issue.title: rust_core_backend_boundary points agents at a nonexistent ../sase-core and omits the linked-repo workflow
issue.description: Core memory rust_core_backend_boundary gives a sibling-path location for sase-core that does not exist from a sase workspace, and never mentions sase repo open, sase-core's AGENTS.md, or the core pin.

task_type_fields.proposed_change:
`rust_core_backend_boundary` (core memory, inlined into every sase agent's instructions) tells agents shared backend logic lives in "the sibling Rust core repo at `../sase-core/crates/sase_core`" and to "update the Rust wire/API, bindings, and tests in `../sase-core`". From a `sase_<N>` workspace no `../sase-core` exists; the only supported path is `sase repo open sase-core` (which yields `sase/repos/linked/sase-core`). sase-14s.1/.2 phase agents first looked for `crates/...` in the wrong place.

Proposed change (keep it short — this is core memory):
- Replace the `../sase-core` paths with "open it with `sase repo open sase-core` and use the printed path".
- Add one line of cross-repo procedure: sase-core's own `AGENTS.md` is not auto-loaded from a sase workspace, so read `<printed path>/AGENTS.md` before editing sase-core; a binding added in sase-core that sase calls requires ratcheting `sase-core-revision.txt` (see `docs/rust_backend.md`, which no memory currently points to).

Related (not the same file): the accepted decision record `decisions:rust-core-required` still quotes the `sase-core-rs` window `>=0.31.0,<0.32.0`; the live window is `>=0.34.70,<0.35.0` (pyproject.toml:48). Because accepted decision records are immutable, decide whether to leave that illustrative number alone or record the window as "owned by publish.yml" rather than a literal.

Found during the sase-core agent-maintainability research (research.24 consolidation).
